known_gap: F-S0-0001 (peer's diagnosis) and F-0007 (master session's finding): the product has no check that compares a part's pin-to-net map against the DESIGN INTENT, and the one check that could (IV.2, against the KiCad symbol) cannot run because part_pinouts.lookup finds no symbol for our MPNs. The board is emitted for fabrication with the transistor wired backwards.
expected_detector: NONE TODAY — this is a named false pass
description: Q1's emitter and collector are transposed. The 2N2222A's pin 1 (emitter) sits on RELAY_COIL_NEG and its pin 3 (collector) sits on GND, where the design says the opposite. The relay coil is then switched from the emitter: drive the base high and the transistor passes as an emitter follower, the coil sees almost no voltage across it, and the relay never actuates. The part also runs reverse-active, where a 2N2222A has a fraction of its rated hFE. The board is silent, undamaged, and completely dead.
seed_target: Q1's pins 1 and 3 in the netlist. The base netlist states the design intent — {1: GND, 2: RELAY_CTRL, 3: RELAY_COIL_NEG} — and the seed transposes pins 1 and 3 to {1: RELAY_COIL_NEG, 2: RELAY_CTRL, 3: GND}. The board is re-derived from the defective netlist by the product's own compile_board, so the copper and the pad map both carry the fault: the result is exactly the board the product would emit for the wrong netlist.
notes: THIS CASE IS A NAMED FALSE PASS AS OF 2026-10-21, and that is the finding, not a gap in the seed. The product's own verifier returns ok=True and the gate says {emit: true, reason: '9 check(s) unproven (unknown rung)'} on the defective board. Nothing flips. The reason is in two places. First, III.4 compares the board's pin-to-net map against THE NETLIST, and the defective board matches the defective netlist perfectly — the check answers 'is the board what we were told to build', not 'is what we were told to build right'. Second, IV.2, 'every part's pinout agrees with the KiCad symbol for its part number', cannot run: part_pinouts.lookup('2N2222A', 'TO-92') finds nothing, because the installed KiCad 10.0 library names the part PN2222A and the lookup has no bridge from one to the other. The verifier says so honestly ('no part could be compared') and stays at the unknown rung, but a rung of unknown is not a failure, so the board passes. The 2N2222A is not the only part affected: 1N4007 matches exactly, ATMEGA328P-PU matches by prefix, and DHT22 and SRD-05VDC-SL-C match nothing at all. A wrong pinout on a transistor is a dead board that every other check passes. It is a critical-class defect class with no check behind it today. Fixing it needs the lookup to reach the KiCad symbol for a part number, and a check that fails a board whose pinout was never compared against a second source — that is the peer's F-S0-0001, and it is the same defect this case was built to expose.
